title: A harder middle pulse in FRB20221129B has window-dependent support in public CHIME intensity data
abstract: We test a fitted spectral reversal in FRB20221129B with public CHIME intensity data. At the catalog dispersion measure, narrow pulse windows give high-band fractions of 0.472, 0.948 and 0.527. A common spectral ratio gives a weighted loss of 40.30, with no exceedances in 10,000 block-noise draws for each of three block lengths. Wider pulse windows reduce the loss to 7.22 and give null-tail fractions of 0.026 to 0.103. Dispersion-measure shifts also change the support. The data give conditional evidence for a harder middle pulse but do not give a stable physical reversal claim across the tested windows and noise rules. The method uses a covariance-whitened rank-one fit and direct band sums, not fitted spectral peaks. It extends an earlier catalog-only test of this event. Short noise records, selected pulse windows, instrument response, and lack of separate telescope data limit the result. Code, inference statistics, a figure, exact input hashes and a retrieval recipe are included. External intensity arrays stay outside the baseline publication. display.caption: Direct band statistics at the catalog DM depend on pulse windows and noise blocks. Error bars show separate 95 percent measurement intervals. Narrow-window tail fractions are simulation floors, not discovery probabilities.
